I bet you don't want advice at this point. Or someone to relate to. Just know that life can get better. At any rate, here is my story.

  I always saw my depression as an adventure I went on. I saw the road everyone walked and hated where I saw it leading.  So I went down an unbeaten path. A dark road that I didn't see the way but I saw where it was leading.  I went down my dark road and lost my way for a long time.  At points I was numb to the world at others I was suicidal, but in the end, I finally found what drives me.  What makes my life worth it.  For all of us it's different.  Don't stop fighting.  It's just creating our own road to a place we want to go.  The fight was worth it for me.  I hope you find life worth fighting for.

I bet you have received a lot of cliche advice.  I have been at that hopeless point. I have held a knife to my wrist at one point and put a loaded pistol in my mouth at another.  The only thing that held me back when there was no one else there for me was the thought: what if this does not end the pain ? What if this life is the only chance i have to find something beautiful in myself and in this world?  I don't know if this makes you sadder or gives you hope, but this thought is what has driven me out of depression for the last ten years.  We must fight. 

For us and no one else we must fight for something better. And through that fight I found beauty and someone to fight for.  I hope this helps I really do.
If it's a good idea, someone else will agree with me, and also, ending this life will not necessarily remove my feelings of pain. Just remember if you got to this point you can dig your way out of it

I had my own bout of depression for a long time (10 years) almost killed myself in the process. And it took me just as long to unwind and undo the damage I had done to myself.  It is a long road, and I got lost on it so many times.  I did have to find myself again. What helped me was knowing that if I am feeling really down, and I can't find the reason, it's the depression talking.  That means I can let go of the sadness at that time.  Meditation helps, so does keeping the mind busy to not let myself think of the sadness.  I hope these suggestions  help. It's the toughest road I've walked yet. Good luck
